idea: Fund manager due diligence for family offices
buyer: Family offices and small institutional allocators
pain: Allocating without the resource to diligence managers properly
channel: Husband's IB and hedge fund network
verdict: Real market with real fees, but she has no manager-selection track record and it is a credentialled niche.

why.distribution: Reachable through her husband's network, but as introductions into a segment she has not sold to.
why.demand: Allocators do pay consultants for this; the market exists and is competitive.
why.fmf: Adjacent, not core. She analysed companies, not fund managers - different diligence discipline entirely.
why.revenue_structure: Repeat purchase as allocations recur, no contract.
why.defensibility: Established consultants own this space and have decades of comparative data she lacks.
why.time_to_revenue: Building credibility in a new discipline first: 3-6 months.
why.tailwind: Family office growth is real but slow.
why.ceiling: £8k x 25 reports = £200k, requiring a volume of allocator relationships she does not have.

ceiling_arithmetic: £8k x 25 manager reports = £200k. Reaching 25 needs 8-10 repeat allocator clients; realistic year one is 4-6 reports = £40k.
carries: Established willingness to pay and decent fees.
kills: Founder-market fit. Company analysis and manager selection look similar and are not, and incumbents have the comparative dataset.
test: Ask two allocators what they currently pay and to whom.
test_pass: They describe an unmet need her company-analysis lens actually addresses.
test_fail: They name Mercer, Albourne or an in-house team.
